raw_sources.provenance_note: Input path and hashes identify the file actually used; the mirror URL is a retrieval option, not a claim this local file was downloaded in this run.

limitations_and_protocol_notes: Paper Table 1 reports 112 skills; upstream prints this after keeping the first row of each order_id and before replacing skills by unique Q-matrix rows.
The full question-to-skill matrix is built before order_id deduplication, so the actual model input contains 149 unique skill combinations for the verified corrected.csv.
The minimum-length filter precedes deduplication in upstream. The verified file therefore retains 51 students with fewer than 5 distinct interactions (minimum 2). This run preserves that order.
The later collapsed one-row-per-student-problem release differs from the expanded corrected.csv used here and should not be substituted silently.

data.sample_comparability: new fixed-seed 5000-student sample; not the paper's exact sample
limitations_and_protocol_notes: Same sorted-user shuffle and first-5000 selection as upstream, now with a recorded seed.
The paper's student IDs and sampling seed are unpublished; this is a new reproducible sample, not its exact sample.
Timestamp strings interpreted as UTC rather than host-local mktime; a common offset does not change sequence order.
Per-user timestamp quicksort, question/skill definitions, ID reindexing and missing-answer filtering follow upstream.
No repeated sampling to force the paper's counts. Training uses the fixed sample for all five folds.

data.sample_comparability: complete public AKT 333-student sequence version; counts match but source/fold identity is not proven
limitations_and_protocol_notes: This is the complete public AKT sequence version, not a DataShop raw export.
Student ID is the zero-based sequence-block index; original anonymous IDs are unavailable.
Within-student interaction order and boundaries are preserved exactly; original timestamps are unavailable.
Timestamp is zero and is a placeholder, not an observed event time.
item_id and skill_id both reference the published exercise token; a separate original question ID is unavailable.
Matching paper counts establishes statistical compatibility, not proof of identical CL4KT author data or folds.
